a.text: In my wardrobe, I have a drawer specifically for collecting medals.

The medal I received upon graduating from Cyr Military College, the fifteen-year service medal from the Defense Forces, the Londinium Freedom Medal awarded to me by City Hall four years ago, after quelling the chaos in the city.

Deeper in the drawer are the remnants of a previous order, passed down through my family. The emblem of the Vieux Vanguard, a piece of brick from Lingones, and a golden cup awarded by His Majesty Corsica I.
The cup is now split into two pieces, and the etchings on top are unclear. However, I remember the layout of each pattern, and the expressions on each relief figure.
This is all that my parents, my uncles, and aunts, all that they hoped for: the glory of Gaul, a glory that cannot be denied, and would never fade.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: ...The cup is quite weighty. You should be able to sell it for a good price. The market for Gaulish pieces has always been brisk.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Even if you just melt the thing and sell it as raw gold, it should be enough for you to easily buy an apartment in the finest part of any city.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Here is the key to my home, keep it. The things are in the wardrobe.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Pick a place and start over. Forget everything that happened this past year, call it a fleeting nightmare.

steps.name: Former Defense Forces Soldier
steps.text: Sir, it was you who saved me when those Sarkaz were chasing me. You hid me in the Defense Forces office.

steps.name: Former Defense Forces Soldier
steps.text: I should be thanking you. I'm no longer a member of the Forces, or your Gaulish compatriot...

steps.name: Former Defense Forces Soldier
steps.text: You didn't have to—

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Take it.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: If you find anything else in the house you like, it's yours. The memories mean little to me anymore.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: You'll want to hide here for a while yet, until the situation stabilizes.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: The Military Commission has disarmed the Defense Forces. As it stands now, you're no different from the Victorian civilians to the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Former Defense Forces Soldier
steps.text: But our comrades are still outside. Some of them are, um, unsettled. I want to save them all...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: They've all been captured.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I handed them over to the Military Commission myself.

steps.name: Former Defense Forces Soldier
steps.text: You what...?

a.text: The anger in his eyes deflates before it can reach a peak.
A coward, I evaluated him as much in the past. He may have had some courage in battle, but ultimately, he is a coward.
He survives here with me in ignominy. He can't be compared to those warriors who resist the Sarkaz.
He could never compare.
Could I?
Hah.
I... don't care.
It's been a long time since I cared.

steps.name: Former Defense Forces Soldier
steps.text: Sir, what... are you going to do next?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: The Sanguinarch of Vampires has been waiting for me for some time.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Stay here. Wait until it's all done before you go.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: If you want to live, you'd best pray that when you open the door, the cheering you hear is Victorians, and not the devils.

a.text: Cheering Victorians...
The first thing that comes to my mind is, surprisingly, that Victoria will win.
No, it's probably just a force of habit. Naturally, I hope that Theresis will win. That's the prerequisite to him restoring Gaul.
All my sacrifices, all my betrayals, all my unforgivable sins were enacted in the service of Gaul.
Yes, of course, I serve... Gaul.
I hope.
Groups of people are led out by the Sarkaz forces, heading for the city walls in the distance.
The Sarkaz intend to fortify Londinium, and I'm afraid the final battle lies right before us.
Do they plan to defend the Victorian capital? Perhaps.
Some of the men cast resentful glances at me. I know them. We once... shared a toast.
No one stops me. The Sarkaz don't care where I'm going.
Even if you open the door for a caged fowlbeast, where can it fly?

steps.text: René Lettou?
I didn't expect to encounter you like this.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: This may be a good sign. At least you haven't been executed by the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Do you have time to chat?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Hm, I know you... You're Clovisia, the little leader of the Self-Salvation Corps, yes?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: We've cleared out all your bases, the remaining forces should have all fled Londinium. Why are you still here?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Some of the thanks go to the Defense Forces, and some go to Caster for keeping her promise.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Her Trilby Asher did indeed ensure the smooth evacuation of the Self-Salvation Corps.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: The Duke of Caster...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: ...I guessed your identity a long time ago. But now, no matter which of the dukes you're vassal or puppet of, I no longer care.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I may not know how capable you really are, but Londinium as she stands is no place for a rebellious child to be wandering around.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Go back to your hiding place. Treasure the fact that the Sarkaz have not caught you yet. I'll pretend I never saw you.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: ...Lettou.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: You've been cowering in Londinium for long enough.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: After losing contact with the Self-Salvation Corps, I quickly found new objectives to work on within Londinium.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: We... were betrayed too. And I don't even know who the traitors were.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: But I don't have time to dwell on that. The situation within the city far surpasses our understanding of a nomadic city under occupation.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: What's happening now is something you won't find in the history books.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I know that better than anyone.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: But have you seen what's going on outside the city?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I've seen the Sarkaz Arts Circles, the red light in the sky, the war machines in their many forms, things unlike the military equipment of any ordinary nation.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I've seen hexcrafters floating in midair, seizing control of the sky, forcing drones and Arts alike to fail.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I used to think the descriptions of the Sarkaz military and the so-called 'Nachzehrer' were tall tales, literary embellishment for horror's sake.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I don't think that anymore.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: When death itself opens its doors, what manmade hell do we face?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: And what of the dukes?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The ducal armies... they're resilient, grand, but...

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: They stand on the horizon, out of reach.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I suppose you may be feeling guilt and melancholy, perhaps mixed with a dash of pride?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: You ponder the cruel choices you've made, but your mission is now accomplished.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I guess you proposed a deal to Theresis regarding the nomadic cities that once belonged to Gaul.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Londinium is too small, she can't contain the Sarkaz ambition. He is simply using this place to provoke the expansionist lust of Terra's other powers.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Do you honestly believe he cares at all for your Gaul?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Londinium's fall is complete, but you are no fool. You see it.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The Military Commission of Kazdel has no intention of occupying Victoria.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Correct, I am no fool. I never once placed my hopes in Theresis keeping his word.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: And yet you still had a hand in so many tragedies.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Are you trying to create an opportunity? Like what the Sarkaz are doing for Kazdel?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Perhaps this war will exhaust the ducal militaries, making space for the ghost of Gaul to return to the land of the living.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: But the question is—

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: —Do you actually believe that, René Lettou?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: What else can I believe in?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I've admitted my weakness. Do you need me to admit my stupidity, my despair, my irrelevance?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: What do you want from me?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Cooperation.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The Self-Salvation Corps, those resisting the Sarkaz, those struggling for survival among Victoria's nonsensical nobility, they all still have a chance.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: And that which you seek, your so-called 'Gaul', may also exist within that chance.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Gaul... oh, Gaul.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: It seems you're still willing to fight.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: For a person like you, the dusty rubble is a platform from which to grab the next ledge.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: For you, those like you, for the Military Commission...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: You are strong enough to subvert a nation, to change the course of history, not to mention... manipulate the fate of one or two men like me.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Enough of the self-pity. There is still much we can do before hell descends upon us.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Whether you consider this a form of atonement or the beginning of a new struggle doesn't matter to me.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: But Lettou, I hope we can—

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Now then, oh great one, can you tell me—

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: How I might save myself?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: There it is. You haven't a clue yourself.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Let me by.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: You really won't turn back?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I won't.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Then I can't say I wish you well.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Your hands are stained with the blood of so many, with the blood of my friends, and you carry on with such despicable decisions.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: René Lettou!

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: That'll do, then. Run along now, the Sarkaz are coming.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I still have... to say goodbye.

a.text: Ces Lingones baignent nos yeux de larmes♪
Le champ de bataille est chargé d'amertume et de peine♪
Mais ce jour viendra, c'est certain♪
Pour juger à mort les agresseurs♪
Pour juger à mort les agresseurs♪
A 'Vieux Vanguard' living in the city.
Why is he the first thing to come to my mind in this moment?

steps.text: ...Name! Rank! Unit!

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Your baton is pressed against my waist rather harshly, sir.
Fermez-la! Report... Name, rank, and unit! Soldat!

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Lingones Youth Vanguards, 2e Régiment de la Garde Sautante, Caporal Lettou!

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: My... unit?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Yes, your unit.

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: I've... never seen you... before.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: You have, you've just forgotten, sir.

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: Have I...?

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: L'Empereur, Sa Majesté, he ordered me to recover here... but... I want to know... what's happening... on the front lines.

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: Le Roi-Sorcier... the wicked Witch King... did our fleet... destroy him?

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: I saw it on television... the Victorian Duke with the great... big... HUGE beard... his army!

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: Do they... wish to betray Sa Majesté... our great Emperor... they will stab him in the back... too?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Sir, Londinium has fallen.

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: C'est bien! Good!

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: I'll be promoted... to the Vieux Vanguard! You... it's not your time yet... you still need... to prove yourself!

a.text: He's nearly ninety years old. He's been not-entirely-there for quite some time, forgetting nearly everything.
For decades, his mind has remained in the golden age when the Gaulishmen joined Corsica I's march into Leithanien.
The nurses always said he had only a year to live, but he's still here.
He's lived to see Gaul become history.
He's lived to Londinium teetering on the edge of her grave.
Before I left the Defense Forces, I issued one last order, to guarantee the safety of this sanatorium.
This is the only thing I did for myself in my entire long service to the Forces.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I brought you a Rheims Champagne, from Lingones. Your favorite. Have a seat, won't you?

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: A fine drink, Caporal, mm...

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: Ces Lingones baignent nos yeux de larmes♪

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: Le champ de bataille est chargé d'amertume et de peine♪

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: ...Pour juger à mort les agresseurs...♪

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: When you sing that song, it's as if there never was any pain, as if you never aged a day.

steps.name: Senile Old Man
steps.text: ...Notre drapeau sera toujours glorieux♪

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I've never seen Lingones.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: You told me again and again about those magnificent halls, the flourishing road networks...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: ...Do you remember Golding, the girl who visited you with me so many years ago?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: She's dead.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: She died for this cruel, unshakeable, bloodstained world.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: And I'm one of the murderers responsible for it all.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I don't know... what to feel for her.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: But she's gone. She's out of my sight, and she'll certainly never see me anymore.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I... I'm frightened, sir.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: A girl called Amiya says that all I've done was done out of cowardice.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I once confessed to Golding that my only goal was to survive the ruin to come.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: But I still hope...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Even if it's just a pretext, I still hope—

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: That from the ruins, a new Gaulishman will rise...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: No, that's not it.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I wish Golding could keep on teaching the children, under the sunshine, among the fragrance of the flowers.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Her persistence was truly beautiful.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: But me, I'm the one who... I'm...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I've done all I can, sir. It's tiring.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Do you think we still have a future?

a.text: He'd fallen asleep minutes ago.
Right then.
I draw my saber. A sword that once belonged to a Gaulishman.
I think... it might be better to let him remain in that dream before the Sarkaz force their way in.
At least it'll be a splendid dream.
But me... despicable man that I am, dare not reach out to pollute—
The blood of the aged Youth Vanguard splatters my hands.
The Prince of Blood himself, the Sanguinarch of Vampires, looks silently at the extravagant decor of the Victorian palace.
The expression on his face could be described as... serene.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You came, Lettou.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Here I thought you'd find somewhere to hide.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: No, of course not.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I was always going to come find Your Highness.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You seem spirited today, I'm pleased. Ever since that old Gaulish teacher of yours died, you've been quite the buzzkill.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: I made a bet with my children, they wagered that you were about to die.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: But I believed in you, Lettou.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Have a drink with me, to the defeat of your enemies, the death of the nation of Victoria.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: I'll begin the ritual myself, bestowing the most ancient curse, the most tragic end.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: And so I will be leaving soon. Even my own kin don't enjoy such an honor, you should be grateful.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: You know, Your Highness...

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: By the time I was born, Gaul's capital had already been razed by the Duke of Wellington and his despicable accomplices.

a.text: A city annihilated, as one breathes a sigh.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Now it seems you will do the same to Londinium.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Will you weep for her?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I just... didn't expect it.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Duke Wellington dismantled Lingones, pulling those mobile plates apart. Heh, so silly, so boring, the Victorians.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Would you like to settle the blood debt with your own hands? I admire your persistence.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: I could grant you such an opportunity.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Your Highness is most magnanimous.

a.text: I bow deeply, but I feel his gaze lingering on me.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Ah... pathetic.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Mean, fickle, cowardly, self-righteous.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Begging for mercy out of fear, self-destructing out of despair.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: But I'm still very curious about you.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: In the scheme of your insignificant life, we've spent quite some time together.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: —Do you really think you can kill me, Lettou?

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You won't.

a.text: My very blood grips my heart.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You may think to yourself, this Sarkaz is so arrogant, so contemptuous.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: On the contrary... Lettou.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Considering what I am about to see, I am positively filled with affection for you.

spans.text: Considering what I am about to see, I am positively

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: You are a fool, yes, and despicable indeed. You should cherish your blood.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: At first, I thought they might have some more interesting uses.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: *Sigh*, such hasty farewells between us.

a.text: The Gaulishman's sword... I do my best to reach it.
The despicable man's sword.

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: Poor man. Keep trying, give it all you've got and you just might reach the hilt.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I'll... grant...

steps.name: Sanguinarch of Vampires
steps.text: What is it you're trying to say?

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I'm saying—

a.text: The blade cuts across my throat, cold, chilling.
I see my filthy blood gushing from my neck.
The crimson liquid stains his clothes and splashes his face.
Hah.

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: I'm saying... I'll... 'grant' you my blood, vile leech!

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: You'll never boast about the purity of your blood ever again!

steps.name: Lt. Colonel Lettou
steps.text: Because the despicable René Lettou has polluted it!
